title: Maximum Candies Allocated to K Children
summary: Given an array of candy pile sizes and an integer k, divide the piles into k groups so that each group has the same total number of candies.
statement: Given an array of candy pile sizes and an integer k, divide the piles into k groups so that each group has the same total number of candies. Some piles may remain unused. Return the maximum number of candies each child can receive.
constraints: A pile may be split into smaller piles, but piles cannot be combined.
Each of k children receives one pile containing the same positive number of candies.
Unused candies are allowed; return zero if every child cannot receive even one.
reference_solution:
def maximum_equal_candy_share(candies,k):
    low,high=1,max(candies);answer=0
    while low<=high:
        middle=(low+high)//2
        if sum(pile//middle for pile in candies)>=k:answer=middle;low=middle+1
        else:high=middle-1
    return answer

hints: For a proposed share x, pile//x portions can be made, and feasibility decreases monotonically as x grows.
Binary-search the largest x whose total portion count is at least k.
Move low above feasible midpoints while saving them; move high below infeasible midpoints.
Monotonicity preserves all possible answers in the search interval, and the final saved feasible midpoint is the maximum equal share.
